top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a distinct, mature and cleanly attributed achievement: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and its realisation at the 10^-18 level, with Ye, independently confirmed in several species and laboratories. The citation can be bounded to leave the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes intact, and the two-name allocation is defensible. P002 is scientifically strong (prediction followed by a surprising, widely reproduced experiment) but the three-name limit leaves the credit gap around Cao and earlier moire band theorists, and the interpretation of the correlated phases is still settling, so I rank it second. No award is third because at least one proposal is clearly prizeworthy.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my documented ties (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur, KTH) are in astroparticle physics and have no apparent link to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer
